To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nature of wheat or corn in the diet has an effect on ruminal digestion and on ruminal microbial ecosystem, but not on total-tract digestion of forage NDF.
the nature of the cereal grain fed to beef cattle affects the digestive process in the rumen, but not in the hindgat, and the digestive process is not affected by the nature of corn grain fed.

the nature of the cereal fed to steers fed a high-concentrate diet had no effect on the total tract digestibility of NDF but that the wheat diet depressed NDF digestibility in the rumen and increased NDF digestibility post rumen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms involved in the negative effect of the nature (wheat vs. corn) of high-grain diets fed to ruminants on the digestion of NDF.
the negative effect of wheat in high-grain diets on rumen fermentation and fiber digestion.
the negative effect of the nature and structure of cereals on fiber digestion in ruminants fed high-grain, high-starch diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in high-grain rations, the negative effects of wheat on ruminal digestion of NFD were not compensated by a higher digestion of NFD in the hindgait.
wheat is a better feedstuff than corn for ruminants, especially when high-grain diets are fed, but that dent corn is a better feedstock for ruminants than flint corn.
the wheat-based diet depressed ruminal digestion of forage, whereas the dent corn-based diet depressed the activity of the solid-associated microbial population in the rumen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nature of wheat or corn used in the diet had no effect on the total-tract digestion of dietary NDF.

the negative effect of wheat on fiber digestion in the rumen can be explained by the low ruminal pH and by the lower fibrolytic activity of the solid-associated bacteria in the rumen, and that the negative effect on fiber digestion of dent corn compared to that of flint corn may be due to a decrease in the fibrolytic enzyme activities of the solid associated bacteria in the ruminal digesta.

the wheat diet was characterized by a high ruminal acidity and a lower ruminal digestion of NFD, whereas the two corn diets were characterized by a high NDF digestibility in the rumen and by a lower NDF digestibility of the hindgut, resulting in a similar NDF digestion at the total-tract level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wheat-based diet depressed NDF digestion more than did the corn-based diets.
the nature of the grain fed to beef steers has a significant effect on the digestive efficiency of fiber in the rumen and the microbial ecosystem of the rumen.
the nature of the grain source has a strong impact on the digestive processes of forage particles.
